ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the diagram, the diagonals $AC$ and $BD$ of square $\square ABCD$ intersect at point $O$. A line $EF\perp AC$ passing through point $O$ intersects $AB$ and $DC$ at points $E$ and $F$, respectively. Lines $AF$ and $CE$ are connected. If $OE= \frac{3}{2}$, what is the length of $EF$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text: \textbf{Solution:} From the given, since $\square ABCD$, we have AO=OC, AB$\parallel$DC, therefore $\angle$FCO=$\angle$EAO, $\angle$CFO=$\angle$AEO, hence $\triangle FCO\cong \triangle EAO$ (AAS), thus FC=AE, therefore quadrilateral AECF is a parallelogram, thus OE=OF=$\frac{1}{2}$EF, since OE=$\frac{3}{2}$, therefore EF=\boxed{3}.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, quadrilateral ABCD is marked as the outline of a tilted square/parallelogram, with A at the lower left, B at the lower right, C at the upper right, and D at the upper left; diagonals AC and BD intersect at the interior point O. There is also a straight line EF passing through O, with the upper end F on side DC and the lower end E on side AB, and at O there is a right-angle mark indicating EF perpendicular to AC; AF and CE are also drawn in the figure. Reasoning: According to the problem statement, ABCD is a square, and O is the intersection point of the two diagonals, so under a 180-degree rotation about O, A maps to C, B maps to D, and side AB maps to side CD. The straight line EF passes through the rotation center O, so this straight line maps to itself under the 180-degree rotation. Point E lies on both AB and EF, so after rotation it must land on the intersection point of CD and EF; in the figure, the intersection point of CD and EF is F. Therefore E maps to F, rotation preserves distance and O does not move, so OE=OF. Also, from the figure E, O, F are collinear and O is between E and F, so EF=OE+OF=2OE=2×(3/2)=3.
